transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I'm mostly here because everybody keeps acting like I'm imagining it. But I'm not. I know my wife's relative came into this house to get at me. 

I mean... my tools don't just move themselves. And my fishing plans don't get spoiled by accident every single weekend. I don't really want to get into all of it right now, but... after all these months, I can see plain as day he's been trying to take over my place. Push me out. 

That's what's going on.

When you think about your wife's relative moving your tools and ruining your fishing plans—do you ever wonder if there might be another explanation, or are you completely certain that he's doing this?

No. I'm certain. 

Look... I know where I leave my things. I work with my hands for a living, I don't just misplace my gear. Like I said, they don't just grow legs and walk away. 

There isn't another explanation. I know he's doing it. I wouldn't be sitting here if I wasn't sure.
How long have you been noticing that your wife's relative has been doing these things to you—weeks, months, or longer?

Months. 

...About nine months, I guess. Pretty much ever since he moved into our house.

During these nine months, have you ever heard voices, seen things, or experienced anything with your senses that others couldn't perceive—or has it mainly been about noticing what he's done to your belongings and plans?

No. I don't hear voices or anything like that. 

...It's just my things being messed with. Like I said. That's it.
If someone you trust—like your wife—told you that she didn't think your relative was moving your things, how would you respond to that?

She does say that. Everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it... I guess that's why I'm here. 

But I know he came into this house to get at me. My tools don’t move themselves. My fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every single weekend. 

...After all these months, I can see it plain as day. He’s been trying to take over my place. Push me out. So... it doesn't really matter what she thinks. I know what's happening.

If I told you that I've reviewed everything you've described, and I couldn't find any evidence that your wife's relative is actually moving your tools or sabotaging your plans, would that change how you think about what's happening—or would you still be convinced he's doing it?

No. It wouldn't change anything. 

Like I just said... I'm only sitting in this chair because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it. But you not finding evidence doesn't mean it isn't happening. 

My tools don’t move themselves. My fishing plans don't just get ruined every single weekend by accident. 

...I see it plain as day. He’s trying to take over my place and push me out. So... no. Whatever you think you reviewed, I'm still convinced. Because I know what he's doing.
You mentioned your wife's relative is trying to take over your place and push you out—can you walk me through how you think he's planning to do that? What's his overall strategy or goal?

I don't know his exact plans. I just know what he's doing. 

...He messes with my stuff. He ruins my weekends. It's just... a way to break me down, I guess. Make me look crazy so my wife kicks me out. 

I haven't sat down and asked him his strategy. I just know he wants me gone. That's all there is to it.

You mentioned he wants to break you down and make you look crazy so your wife kicks you out—but why do you think he wants you gone in the first place? What's his reason for wanting you out of the house?

I don't know. ...You'd have to ask him. 

I just know he wants the place. I don't... I don't sit around trying to figure out why he is the way he is, or what his big reasons are. 

He just wants me gone. That's all I know.
When your fishing plans get ruined on the weekend, how do you know for certain that your wife's relative did it—what specifically tells you it was him and not just bad luck or coincidence?

...I just know. It's not coincidence. You don't just... have bad luck every single time. 

I don't have a camera set up to catch him, if that's what you mean. It's just obvious. ...I don't really know what else to tell you.

You've mentioned he wants to break you down and make you look crazy so your wife will kick you out—and that he wants to take over your place. Do you think there are other things he might be doing to you beyond moving your tools and ruining your fishing plans? Or is it mainly just those two things?

...Mainly just what I told you. 

I don't know if he's doing other things. I haven't... I don't sit around keeping a list of every little thing. It's just the tools and my weekends. 

That's enough, isn't it? I haven't really noticed anything else.

You mentioned your wife's relative moved in about nine months ago—right around when all this started. Before he moved in, did you have any concerns about him, or did these problems with your tools and fishing plans only begin after he arrived?

...No, I didn't have any problems with him before. 

We didn't really see him much. It all just... started when he got here. About nine months ago, like I said. That's when he moved in. 

Before that, everything was fine. It's just been these last nine months.

You've told me he wants to break you down and make you look crazy so your wife kicks you out, and that he wants to take over your place. How do those two goals connect together in your mind—do you see them as part of one overall plan, or are they separate things he's trying to do?

...It's the same plan. Obviously. He pushes me out, he gets the house. 

I mean... I'm only even here talking to you because everybody keeps acting like I'm imagining it. But I'm not. I know he came into this house to get at me. 

My tools don't move themselves. My fishing plans don't get spoiled by accident every weekend. 

After all these months... I can see plain as day he's been trying to take over my place and push me out. That's how it connects. It's just... what he's doing. I don't really have anything else to add to it.
When you think about your wife's relative and what he's doing—do you believe he has special powers or abilities that help him do these things to you, or is he just using ordinary means?

...No. No special powers. 

He's just... a guy. He just waits until I'm not looking, or when I'm out of the room. It's just normal stuff. 

I don't know why you'd ask about special powers. He's just doing things behind my back. That's all.
Besides your wife's relative, do you believe anyone else in your life is working against you or trying to harm you in any way?

...No. Just him. 

I don't... I don't have problems with anyone else. Just the guy living in my house. That's it.

You've told me your wife's relative wants to push you out so he can take over the house—but I'm curious: do you think he's acting alone, or do you believe there's a larger reason or pattern behind why he's targeting you specifically? Is there something about you, or something you have, that makes you the target?

...No. He's acting alone. 

I don't know what you mean by a larger reason. There's no... big pattern or anything. 

He just wants a free place to live. My place. There's nothing special about me, I just... I have a house, and he wants it. That's all there is to it.

When you think about everything your wife's relative is doing—moving your tools, ruining your fishing plans, trying to push you out—do these things all fit together as part of one clear plan that makes sense, or does it sometimes feel like separate things happening that don't quite connect?

...It's a plan. 

He wants me gone. So... he does things to make me look crazy, or make me angry. 

It all connects. He's just... trying to get rid of me.

When your wife's relative moves your tools or ruins your fishing plans—is he doing things that a regular person could actually do if they wanted to, or are the things happening to you physically impossible in some way?

...No. It's not impossible. 

I don't know why you'd ask that. He just... he walks into the garage and moves my tools. Anyone with hands can do that. 

There's no magic to it or anything. He's just a guy doing things behind my back. That's all.
